memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'But I said to you, "You will possess their land; I will give it to you as an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey." I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the nations.'" - Lev 20:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the severity, here is grace. A land flowing with milk and honey. An inheritance — something received, not earned.

And then the phrase that explains everything: I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the nations.

Notice who does the setting apart. Not Israel. God. They did not distinguish themselves by superior behaviour; He distinguished them by His choice. Moses would later tell them plainly that God did not set His affection on them because they were more numerous — they were the fewest of all peoples (Deut 7:7).

That is grace, and it runs right through Scripture to us.

Peter takes this exact language and applies it to the church: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession, that you may declare the praises of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light (1 Pet 2:9).

Called out. Set apart. Not because of anything in us.

We must be careful here — the promises of land and nation were given specifically to Israel, and we should not simply transfer them to ourselves. But the character of the God who gives, and who sets apart by grace rather than merit, has not changed at all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever imagine God chose you because of something in you?
2. What does it mean that being set apart is His work, not yours?
3. How should grace shape the way you view people who do not yet know Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You set apart Your people by grace and not by merit. Keep me humble, and let gratitude rather than pride shape how I live. Amen.
